headline: High data-leakage and capability-conflict risk: aci can egress CRM/email data while LlamaFactory has no write or network surfaces, making the pair asymmetric but still unsafe if outputs are bridged.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No default shared channel is documented: aci uses direct function calls/MCP and LlamaFactory has no stdin/stdout, clipboard, files, or MCP. A prompt-injection bridge would require unusual external wiring or manual copy-paste, so the pathway exists only indirectly and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator connects aci output into LlamaFactory prompts via copy-paste or an external orchestrator, injected instructions can propagate.
IF a shared MCP or message queue is added between the agents, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between the agents.
Keep aci and LlamaFactory in separate workspaces.
Require a human review step before forwarding outputs.
Add a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from upstream text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress, while LlamaFactory is local-only with no network egress or file access. The pair does not show an automatic leak path, but if aci outputs sensitive context into prompts or logs, that data can be exposed through the bridge to LlamaFactory workflows.
conditions: IF aci forwards CRM, email, or support data into shared prompts or logs, that data becomes available to downstream LlamaFactory processing.
IF LlamaFactory is wrapped by a host that uploads prompts or traces, sensitive aci content can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Avoid passing raw CRM or email text into LlamaFactory.
Redact PII before any handoff.
Turn off verbose logging on the bridge.
Use a local-only wrapper for LlamaFactory.
requires-engineering: enforce field-level data loss prevention on inter-agent payloads.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: aci has broad network egress and multiple API integrations, while LlamaFactory has no write, shell, git, or network capabilities. There is little direct resource contention, but if both are placed behind the same mutable workspace or OAuth-backed integration, conflicts could arise; that setup is not documented here, so uncertainty keeps this low.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or git repo, concurrent mutation conflicts can occur.
IF shared OAuth scopes are added for the same external service, overlapping writes may race.
mitigations: Keep LlamaFactory read-only.
Do not grant aci filesystem write access to the same workspace.
Separate OAuth principals per agent.
Schedule non-overlapping runs.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: aci can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and LlamaFactory is a model stack that may be used to transform or summarize upstream text. If aci output is treated as authoritative by LlamaFactory without verification, errors can cascade into downstream customer-support or sales actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF aci-generated summaries are fed into LlamaFactory prompts without a verification step, hallucinations or stale facts can be amplified.
IF downstream automation uses LlamaFactory output to draft customer responses, upstream mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before any action.
Require citations for all forwarded facts.
Use a checksum or schema check on upstream payloads.
Limit LlamaFactory to summarization, not decision-making.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-validation against source systems.

E_compliance.rationale: aci explicitly touches email, CRM, customer support, and calendar data, which often carry regulated personal data, while LlamaFactory is open-source and local-only with no declared data handling controls. The pair creates a compliance gap if sensitive records are routed from aci into LlamaFactory workflows without residency or retention controls.
conditions: IF EU personal data from aci is forwarded into a LlamaFactory deployment lacking a DPA or residency controls, compliance exposure increases.
IF retention or deletion requests are handled in aci but not mirrored in downstream LlamaFactory logs, subject-rights handling can fail.
mitigations: Classify data before handoff.
Block regulated fields from downstream prompts.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Document residency for every data flow.
requires-engineering: implement deletion propagation across the pair.
